why: NCCL does not exist on Windows; one-process group init before any model is loaded.

Low-VRAM branch (free VRAM <= 60 GB) lacked the two upstream FramePack lines that place the text encoders before encoding; without them input ids go to CPU while the swapped embedding weights are on the GPU (device mismatch at C3 on Kaggle T4).
Same fix for the per-section prompt encode inside the generation loop.

Tesla T4 (sm_75) has no flash/mem-efficient bf16 SDPA kernel; the math fallback tried to allocate 30 GiB for the score matrix (C3 OOM, 2026-11-22). Query chunking computes the same softmax(QK^T)V per query row; only the memory layout changes. Inactive on sm_80+ unless ATTN_Q_CHUNK is set.

Tesla T4 (sm_75) emulates bf16: the bf16 dry run took 8358 s for a 2 s clip (C3, 2026-11-22). fp16 uses the T4 tensor cores. Off unless PILOT_TRANSFORMER_DTYPE=fp16; the value used is recorded in each attempt log.

fp16 dry run on the T4 gave an all-black clip: the NaN probe (gen/nan_probe.py) showed the first Inf in transformer_blocks.7's residual add, with finite sub-layer outputs (<= 1940) but a residual stream already at 29760 (hidden) / 51328 (text). Large residual channels are a property of this model family. Residual kept in fp32, the gated residual updates computed in fp32, and the three projections that write into the residual (MLP down-projections, single-block proj_out) return fp32 from fp16 operands; other matmuls stay fp16. Inactive in bf16.
